Tagcast 0.10.0 adds a search across all your tracks, shows multi-disc sets as one
album and can move tracks to iBroadcast's trash after a review.

## What's new

- **Tracks:** a new page in the sidebar searches every track by title, artist, album or composer. Case and accents don't count, so `bjork` finds Björk. Play a track with the rest of its album after it, or open its album with the track marked. The local server searches the library it already holds, so a search asks iBroadcast for nothing.
- **Multi-disc sets as one album:** with iBroadcast's **Combine Multi-Disc Album Sets** off, discs with the same title and album artist show as one album, with a CD icon per disc. The album page lists each disc in its own block, and the editor saves a change to every disc. One cover can be chosen for the whole set.
- **Move to trash:** on an album page, choose **Move to trash…**, tick tracks (or **Select extra copies** of duplicate tracks, or **Select all**), review them and confirm. Tagcast first checks that the tracks are still on that album in iBroadcast, then moves them to iBroadcast's trash. Nothing is deleted permanently, and Tagcast can't take tracks back out of the trash.
- **New filters:** albums with **duplicate tracks** (the same title twice in one album), and album artists **without an image**.
- **Per page:** choose 24, 50, 100 or 200 albums or album artists per page (Tracks: 50, 100 or 200). Tagcast remembers the choice in this browser.
- **Back and Forward:** every page has its own address. The browser's Back and Forward buttons, and **← Back** on a page, return to where you came from with its search, filter and page.
- **Sidebar:** Album artists, Albums, Tracks, Overview and History. Tagcast opens on Album artists.

## Removed

- **Import library JSON.** Tagcast works with your live iBroadcast library, or with the built-in demo when no account is connected.

## Compatibility and validation

- Keep **Combine Multi-Disc Album Sets** off in iBroadcast. With it on, iBroadcast refuses album changes; the README explains why.
- The first track search after a library download builds a search list: about 2 seconds and 50 MB for 288,000 tracks (measured on a generated library). Later searches take about a tenth of a second.
- Python tests, Ruff, JavaScript parsing, frontend regression tests and start-script checks run in CI on Linux, macOS and Windows. Track search, disc sets and the trash were also checked in a browser against a fake iBroadcast server, and tried on a real library.

## Downloads and updating

Stop the currently running Tagcast server. Download the ready-made **Assets**
package for Apple Silicon (`macos-arm64.zip`), Intel Mac (`macos-x64.zip`),
Windows (`windows-x64.zip`) or Linux (`linux-x64.zip`). Extract it and open
`tagcast` (`tagcast.exe` on Windows). These 0.10.0 programs open a console and
then your browser; close the console or use Ctrl+C to stop the server.
Python and dependencies are included; no Python or uv installation is needed.

Alternatively, download **Source code (zip)**, unpack it into a new folder and
run the usual start script. Source installations require Python 3.11+ or uv.
The page should show **0.10.0**. Starting a second copy while the old server is
running opens that old instance instead.

Your account settings and sign-in remain in `~/.tagcast/`, or your configured
`TAGCAST_HOME`. Tagcast does not modify local music files.
